messages.subject: Re: camopPlot function
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nubia,
run the following code in your R console (from the data extraction vignette <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/DataExtraction.html#camera-operation>):
camopPlot <- function(camOp){

  which.tmp <- grep(as.Date(colnames(camOp)), pattern = "01$")
  label.tmp <- format(as.Date(colnames(camOp))[which.tmp], "%Y-%m")
  at.tmp <- which.tmp / ncol(camOp)

  image(t(as.matrix(camOp)), xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n", col = c("red", "grey70"))
  axis(1, at = at.tmp, labels = label.tmp)
  axis(2, at = seq(from = 0, to = 1, length.out = nrow(camOp)), labels = rownames(camOp), las = 1)
  abline(v = at.tmp, col = rgb(0,0,0, 0.2))
  box()
}

Now you an use the function, e.g.:

camopPlot(camOp = camop_problem)

Note that the colors may differ from the example in the vignette if you have stations with 2 or more cameras.
Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Error library(camtrapR)
messages.body_plain:
Dear Nubia,
the error message means that a package camtrapR needs (taxize) is not available on that computer.
You could installing camtrapR the package again.

install.packages("camtrapR")

Normally other packages that camtrapR depends on should be installed automatically (that is the default of install.packages)
If it doesn't, install the missing package with

install.packages("taxize")

Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: UNABLE TO GET CAMERA OPERATION MATRIX DATA
messages.subject_clean: UNABLE TO GET CAMERA OPERATION MATRIX DATA
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nubia,
you're right, argument StationCol is missing. In that case, it will default to

StationCol = "Station"

(see ?cameraOperation).

In your data, the field is called "LOCATION", so your function call should be:

camop <- cameraOperation(CTtable = cams,

                setupCol         = "DATE_SETUP",
                retrievalCol     = "DATE_RETRIEVAL",
                dateFormat       = "%m/%d/%Y",
                stationCol       = "LOCATION")

Alternatively, rename the column in your data to "Station" (without the quotation marks).
Best,
Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: Detection History, "out dir" argument
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nubia,
try
outDir = "C:/Users/NZLR/Documents/CARLOS/ultima base"

Those two forward slashes in the beginning of the argument should not be there.
You can always see if the folder exists by running:

dir.exists("C:/Users/NZLR/Documents/CARLOS/ultima base")

Or simply copy the folder name (in your example:  C:/Users/NZLR/Documents/CARLOS/ultima base) to the address bar of your windows file explorer.

Reversely, to specify the argument correctly, you can open the desired folder in Windows file explorer and copy the folder name from the adress field and paste it as outDir argument (with quotation marks)

Best regards,
Jürgen

messages.subject: geographical position data from Excel
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
You can use any format as long as it's numeric and consistent between stations. The best, globally valid standard would be lat/long in WGS84 coordinate system. Use decimal degrees, not degree minute second format.
UTM coordinates also work fine as long as all stations are within the same UTM zone. Please note the UTM zone must be known for these coordinates to make sense.
You can always convert coordinates, e.g with the R function spTransform.
Try to avoid obscure coordinate systems, sometimes the coordinate conversions may fail.
Best,
Jürgen
